utterances.text: My message is simple.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: I want to see revenue from the pied-a-terre tax go to schools and child care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: Properly funded, the school where my son teaches in Queens could more meaningfully support all students in growing and learning to the best of their abilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: More funding could mean hiring more teachers in lower class sizes, in accordance with the law, which is not being followed now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: More tutoring hours for students.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: As it is now, my son often tries to fill the gaps on his own time with extra tutoring.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: Teaching teenagers isn't as stressful as the lack of resources for public school teachers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: Some of his students are also unhoused.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: The cost of childcare is one of the causes of homelessness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: With free childcare, hopefully we will no longer have nearly one in seven students living in homeless shelters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: On a personal level, I want my son to be able to continue to live in the city where he was born and raised.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: I want to be near my grandchildren.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: Taxing the rich is extremely popular among working New Yorkers, as is our mayor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: Whenever I wear this Tax the Rich t-shirt, people on the street smile or say, I like your shirt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: We who live, work, and pay taxes here year-round make this city a desirable place to have a second home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: It seems reasonable and fair to ask those who don't pay full-time income taxes here, but who have luxury homes here for pleasure, to contribute to the well-being of New York City, its families, and students.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: I

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: really, really hope that the problems in implementation can be resolved so that those who are able and willing to pay taxes on their second pleasure homes

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: are able to do it so that we can have the revenue for really important public services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Beverly Solo
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to speak as a private citizen not representing any organization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Champany
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Champany
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry, a PhD candidate and Washington Heights resident, supports the tax citing research that urban property value is socially produced. She argues the current system taxes the wealthiest the least and that two-thirds of voters support higher taxes on millionaires.
chapters.title: Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry testifies on social contract and wealth inequality

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: Hi.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: My name is Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: I'm a PhD candidate and researcher at the University of California, Berkeley, and I study public finance, land and property taxation, and city planning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: I'm also a Colombian-born Washington Heights resident, living on a graduate student budget, working multiple jobs, and even then, after paying rent and basic expenses, there's not a lot of money left.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: I strongly support the pied-a-terre tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: My research has taught me that a city's fiscal system is more than an accounting mechanism.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: It's an expression of a social contract.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: I've also learned that there's a surprising consensus in orthodox economics on what makes land and property valuable, and it's not the property owners.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: A $5 million or $200 million apartment, say, overlooking Central Park, is worth that much because it overlooks Central Park, because of our parks and subway systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: public investments and its proximity to Wall Street, and because this is a productive and unique city that millions of people make run.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: In other words, urban property value is socially produced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: And precisely for this reason, it's entirely reasonable that those who can most afford to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: Those who not only own a $5 million property, but own more than one, should return that value to the public that helped create it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: Unfortunately, our current property system does the exact opposite.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: We tax the wealthiest the least.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: The city's own reform commission found that a $500,000 home could face more than three times the effects of

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: effective tax rate than a $5 million one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: I ask you, what kind of social contract does that reveal?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: And is that the social contract that you want to uphold?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: New Yorkers know what they want.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: Two recent polls found that roughly two-thirds of New York City voters support higher taxes on millionaires.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: And economists also agree.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: Land taxes do not dampen economic activity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: The rich are the residents least likely to leave New York, according to the Fiscal Policy Institute.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: And even the economists called this a gentle tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: They also know that an economically successful city requires public investments rather than a few slightly wealthier millionaires.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: I should also add that I'm a little shocked that the foundation of local public investment property taxes is being referred to in these

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: proceedings by city councilors as a hit list, a scarlet letter, a security threat, or a form of eminent domain.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: I'm sympathetic to the concerns over difficulties over implementation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: I myself have spent months observing assessors and bureaucrats who implement property taxes as part of my research.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: I also know that if this tax is blocked or significantly delayed because of the minutia of the rollout, which perhaps does have problems, New Yorkers will see these hurdles exactly for what they are,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: ideologically motivated and meant to protect private wealth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: If we want New York to remain a city for teachers, families, and everyone else who makes it run, not simply a place to store wealth,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: We need a tax system that reflects that social contract.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Pena-Randa-Curry
utterances.text: I expect the City Council to stand by that and to support the pied-a-terre tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Champany
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Champany
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Dave Backer, a parent and school finance professor, supports the surcharge and argues the real problem is the property tax system's structure. He notes 43% of school funding comes from property taxes and that single-family homeowners pay 2.4 times less than multifamily dwellers.
chapters.title: Dave Backer testifies in support of tax for school funding and child care

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: Hi, Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: My name is Dave Backer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: I'm a parent of a six-year-old who's going to first grade at PS20 in Brooklyn, and a nine-month-old who I'm hoping will go to 2K after that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: I'm also a co-op owner, and I was excited about the rollout of this surcharge.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: I didn't feel fear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: I didn't feel nervousness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: I didn't feel any panic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: At all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: In fact, I was excited about it, and I was excited about it for a lot of the reasons that the last speaker just said.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: I happen to be a professor of school finance as well, and I know that the real problem

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: here is not necessarily the rollout, but the way that the property tax system is structured and the way in which our kids'schooling and child care is all reliant upon it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: This real problem, 43% of the money that goes to our kids'schools and child care comes from revenues brought in from property.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: Now, we have a trillion dollars of market value in this city that we could tax, but we're only at about a fifth of it in what we actually assess.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: We're falling short there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: Single family homeowners, as the last speaker just mentioned, actually already pay 2.4 times less in their effective tax rate than multifamily dwellers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: So my partner and I actually moved out of New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: We went to a more affordable city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: We had our daughter, and when we heard that pre-K was...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: coming out, we were like, wow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: We looked at the numbers, and it turned out we could save $60,000 a year by moving back to New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: So we moved back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: We came back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: And we want that for everybody in this city, and we want to keep building on it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: I think the wealthy homeowners here doth protest a little too much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: And I really hope that this debate, quote unquote, actually doesn't get in the way of much needed revenue in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dave Backer
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Champany
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Laila Pinaranda, a CUNY staff member and union member, supports the tax arguing housing should be for living, not parking wealth. She urges the council to stand with public sector workers and ensure the wealthiest contribute to public institutions like CUNY.
chapters.title: Laila Pinaranda testifies in support of tax for CUNY and public services

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Champany
utterances.text: Next.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair and members of the City Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: My name is Laila Pinaranda, and I'm here today as a worker, a co-op resident, and a public sector union member to speak in support of the Piedad Terra tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: Today, we stand under the emblem, a government of the people, for the people, by the people, a principle which should hopefully inform today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: I am a full-time CUNY staff member, a member of the PSC CUNY Union, a researcher at the CUNY Research Foundation, and a CUNY alum.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: Everything I am, I am thanks to CUNY and public education institutions of New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: CUNY, as well as many public services, are the infrastructure that makes private and commonwealth possible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: The question before us is simple.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: Who should pay for that infrastructure?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: I believe those who have accumulated the greatest wealth

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: should contribute the greatest share.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: That is not an attack, contrary to what we've heard today, on ordinary homeowners.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: It is a recognition that housing should be a place to live, not simply another vehicle for accumulating and parking wealth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: As a CUNY worker, I see every day what public investment makes possible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: CUNY is one

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: of the great democratic institutions of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: It gives working class New Yorkers like myself access to education, research, economic opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: But higher education has been asked to do more and more while operating under enormous financial pressure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: And CUNY is only one example.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: Our public institutions are the common wealth of the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: We should reject the idea that government must constantly make working class people choose between the services that allow for dignified life and other basic necessities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: The wealth exists.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: Today's city council hearing asks, are we visionary, bold, and courageous enough to organize our tax system so that wealth contributes to the society that produces and sustains it?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: I urge the city council to stand with public sector workers and stand with CUNY.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: City council, stand for the principle that the wealthiest among us should pay their fair share.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laila Pinaranda
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Brewer clarifies that she, Chair Lee, and the Speaker support the pied-à-terre tax, noting the Speaker initially suggested it to the state. She emphasizes the hearing is about implementation challenges, not the tax itself, then calls the next panel.
chapters.title: Brewer clarifies council support for the tax and calls next panel

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We always stand with CUNY, I want you to know.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: But also, many of us, the speaker and certainly both co-chairs and many of the members support this tax.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I want to be very, very...

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: very clear and the speaker was the one who suggested it initially to the state.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So it's the tax we are for.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It's the implementation that has some challenges, but I just want to make that clear.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Some members may disagree, but I want you to know that Councilmember Lee and I in particular support this tax, just so you're clear.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I don't think there's any questions.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So next panel.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you all.

chapters.summary: Lucy Sexton of New Yorkers for Culture and Arts supports the tax but asks for an exemption for Joint Live Work Quarters for Artists (JLWQA) units used for nonprofit arts production. She shares the case of a dancer whose inherited Soho loft faces a $90,000 surcharge.
chapters.title: Lucy Sexton testifies on impact on artist JLWQA spaces in Soho

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Lucy Sexton, Ed Lee, June Barwick, and Ken Fisher.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Go ahead and start.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Lucy, you want to start?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: Hi.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: My name is Lucy Sexton.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: I lead New Yorkers for Culture and Arts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: It is a coalition of hundreds of artists and cultural organizations of all sizes across the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: I am here to talk about the impact of this law's effect on artists.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: I want to also start by saying that I have long supported and been in favor of a pied-a-terre tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: I lived in Soho for some time, and it was distressing to see that neighborhood with dark windows at night.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: No families, no people living there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: It really hollowed out the neighborhood and skewed those prices.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: So while I'm in favor of it, I'm asking the city council to address one particular part of it, which is that the artists who moved into Soho and other places in the 70s and transformed industrial spaces.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: Were at threat of that they shouldn't live there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: So the city council came up with the joint living and work quarters assignment for those units, which meant that they were going to work there, they're going to rehearse there, they're going to do dance class there, and they're also going to live there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: Well, right now I have a member of my organization who his parents were very famous.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: Postmodern dancers David Gordon and Valda Satterfield established their loft in Soho in 1976.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: They died recently, and he now owns it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: He is continuing to use it, as he has for 40 years, as a place for his theater company to rehearse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: He gives it out at low to no cost to dance companies, for dance classes, for performances.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: It is in heavy use.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: He got a notice that he has to pay $90,000.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: He makes less than that in a year, so this will wipe him out and force him to sell the unit if it goes through.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: I'm asking that the council look at the joint live and work quarters, JLQUA, whatever it's called,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: and make a special exception to say, yes, if it is being used for nonprofit art use, if it is being actively

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: rented and rented, particularly rented at much below market cost to artists to live, work, and create work in, that that should also be a reason that they should be able to hold on to that unit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: The city council stepped in the 70s to protect them and make sure they could stay there at this time when artists'housing and artists'workspace is in woefully short supply and we are barely able to make a living and live here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: Do everything you can to protect spaces that they must be able to prove it but are still being used for nonprofit arts production and rehearsal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucy Sexton
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Next.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Don't take a knee.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Pressure button.

chapters.summary: Ed Lee, identifying as Republican, expresses support for the tax in spirit but criticizes the city for not spending money correctly. He discusses homelessness, city agency failures, CUNY spending, and argues the city should fix broken systems before raising new taxes.
chapters.title: Ed Lee testifies against tax, citing government corruption and misplaced priorities

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: Hi, how's it going?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: My name's Ed Lee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: As a Republican, I don't take a knee-jerk reaction to everything Mondani says and say that it's bad.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: I'm with the Peter tax in spirit because we know that the rich, you know, use tax shelters like capital gains and dividends and pay proportionally less than the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: And I'm for fair treatment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: By the way, Trump has done significant work to prevent people from hiding money overseas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: But this tax unfairly targets people who choose real estate versus other industries such as securities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: Family assets will be impacted also.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: What are the taxes spent on?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: Is this really for the little people or is this just one set of aristocrats attacking another set of aristocrats but now with fancy marketing language?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: I see a wolf versus a wolf in sheep's clothing and the wolves in sheep's clothing honestly spill more blood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: I'm homeless right now because the not-for-profit system picks winners and losers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: I work with the longest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: Wrongfully incarcerated man in New York State history, Otis Johnson, the parents of Gams and Tron, whose death caused the resignation of CEO and chair of NYCHA, Gregory Russ, a disabled victim of deep theft, terrorized by a tax-sponsored anti-violence group who is here speaking later today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: I have extensive documentation of city agencies and funded not-for-profits, not just ignoring my coalition, but actively raising barriers and interfering with our quest for justice, sometimes even violently assaulting members of my coalition with no acknowledgement or consequences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: Private universities don't pay property taxes while they destroy the financial futures of our children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: Maybe they should be considered to pay property taxes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: What prevents this from happening?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: A 2016 Inspector General report found that CUNY spent significant resources on outside contracts, including for lobbyists engaged in questionable...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: and seemingly redundant tasks despite also employing its own central and school-based government relations staff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: PSC, a highly visible electoral action group, which is primarily unionized college professors, is asking for more federal research dollars while Jeff Parsons, who was the driving force behind gender-neutral bathrooms, was having cocaine parties and sexually harassing staff and misusing federal research dollars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: I hold New York City's only third-party independent can debates, and every participating candidate in the 2025 election cycle has asked for a public meeting between myself, Corey Edens, and the CUNY Chancellor, as well as Hunter College President.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: Diner, I would appreciate your help on that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: City agencies and NFPs have consistently let us down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: Before the city raises new taxes, the city should refocus their efforts on fixing the broken and corrupt system that pays homeless shelter executives more than the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: President.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: My fellow homeless people are dying protesting the violent and dysfunctional self-serving city services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: Gavin's parents have left this city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: They're now in Florida disgusted by the lack of care for their issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: Thank you for listening, and God bless.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ed Lee
utterances.text: I know there's a lot of well-meaning stuff behind this tax, but you're not spending the money right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Champany
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Champany
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: June Borwick, treasurer of a small Nolita co-op, raises concerns about co-ops being valued at only 20% of single-family homes, the retroactive nature of the tax, and the unfairness of co-op units being discriminated against versus single-family homes. She calls for an exemption for mid-range co-ops.
chapters.title: June Borwick testifies on co-op valuation disparities and retroactive concerns

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: My name is June Borwick.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: I'm the treasurer of a small self-managed building in Nolita.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: We have four units.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: It's unclear, like it is for many people, which of those will have to pay the tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: But they each will have to pay, if they do have to pay, almost as much as the whole building pays, which is completely unfair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: Part of that, most of that, is due to the rather unusual decision made that somehow co-ops are valued at only 20% of single-family homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: We get values on our property taxes, on the notice of property values, and so on, and we know roughly what those values are, and there is no way that our building, despite being a beautiful landmark, is worth $44 million, which is what the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: de facto...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: Jump of five times for a co-op building for each unit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: I have a couple problems about the tax, most of which I suspect nothing can be done about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: The idea of a retroactive tax where it's kind of an unhappy surprise that something that happened last January

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: is what defines what has to happen to you next year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: The second thing is,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: It's somewhat of a surprise to have a real estate tax being based on market value, not assessed value, both in New York City and elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: But the third thing, and the thing that might be actionable in some way by the city council or by the Department of Finance, is that there ought to be some kind of exemption.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: That enables a co-op that is worth, theoretically, by market value, between, let's say, a million and two million, which sounds like a lot of money.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: Frankly, to me, it is a lot of money, can be shown to have a specific market value.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: And once they have that, they can be put into the class of

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: single and two and three family homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: We live in co-ops.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: They are single family homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: Why there's a discrimination between us and the other single family homes is really kind of beyond me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: Most people who live in a co-op or a condo have a reasonable idea of what their market value is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: And anybody who's either the treasurer or the property manager of the building knows what the market, the assessed value of these buildings are.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: And I think those should be used.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - June Borwick
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Champany
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Champany
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: A panelist shares two personal cases: his own apartment at 733 Park Avenue where a neighbor received his surcharge notice by mail, and his son's trust-held apartment. He describes website errors preventing him from contesting the notice and questions his due process rights.
chapters.title: Unnamed panelist testifies on personal surcharge notice and botched process

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: First of all, I'd like to thank the committee very much for holding this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And I'm wondering, before I even give my testimony, what power does this committee even have to assist?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: in the implementation of this tax?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Can anybody answer?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I mean...

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We have oversight responsibility, and certainly the fact that you're all here gives us even more ammunition to question the implementation.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So it's a process, but we are going to get answers to the questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: So, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I'd like to relate to you two cases today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The first case is for my own apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I live at 733 Park Avenue, floor 29.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I've lived in this apartment full time since 2018 and have always filed New York City and New York State tax returns.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And I'd like to add for the record that I pay a ton of tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: When I was in the elevator going to my apartment, I just happened to bump into a neighbor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: He informed me that he had received my non-primary residence property surcharge notice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I was shocked.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: He showed me a copy and I took a cell phone picture of it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: My apartment was clearly listed on the notice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: However, my neighbor's name and his wife's name were the addressees on the notice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The post office had delivered the notice to his apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: If I hadn't run into my neighbor in the elevator that day, I never would have even known about this matter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: So I gathered my documents to prove my primary residence, such as my shareholder certificate, my tax returns showing my address, and my driver's license.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: When I went into the website at first, the website would not let me proceed, claiming incorrect PIN.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I tried several times and it would not let me proceed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: So I put it aside and I decided to give it a try another day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Yesterday, I tried again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: This time, the PIN worked.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: However, my apartment was marked as filed and it would not let me proceed or submit any documents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: At this point, I have no way of objecting to the non-primary residence notice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: So I think that this entire process has been completely botched.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Am I not entitled to due process?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Am I just supposed to pay a tax of $58,479 without at least having an opportunity to rebut it, to prove that I live in this apartment?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: That's case number one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Case number two relates to my son's apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: In 2012, I established a trust for the benefit of my daughter and my son.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: We purchased an apartment right down the street from me for my son to live in, and he lives there full time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: He got the same notice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Now, under the law, the rule is that if you are the sole beneficiary of the trust, you can contest that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: But if there are two people that are beneficiaries, you can't contest it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Now, in this instance, unfortunately, my daughter passed away, so we will be able to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And test that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: But it's such an unfair thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: You know, we set up that trust in 2012.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Here we are in 2026 with a law that applies prospectively, not retroactively.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: It's just so unfair.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We will be glad to offline to set you up with somebody at finance if you want, particularly for case one and if you need for case two.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: By the way, I did file a complaint with finance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: checked my cell phone while it was waiting to testify today, and they replied a very truncated answer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: All it said was, withdraw the prior submission and resubmit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Now, I didn't submit the first submission.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, but we'll be glad to help you with that, just so you know.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: All right?

chapters.summary: Lee thanks the panel and announces the next panel: Clara Calvo, Brandon Rango, Jamel Henderson, and Kay Presley.
chapters.title: Chair Lee dismisses panel and calls next panel

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you very much, panel.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Clara Calvo, Brandon Rango, Jamel Henderson, and Kay Presley.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you for being here.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Whoever would like to start.

chapters.summary: Katie Ann Presley describes a deed theft case where an individual took over her building, harassed and assaulted residents, and shut off utilities. She reports a probable cause finding from the Division of Human Rights and asks the committee to investigate deed theft.
chapters.title: Katie Ann Presley testifies on deed theft case and domestic terrorism

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: Yes, hi, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: My name is Katie Ann Presley.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: I am a resident of New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: I'm here because my case is relevant not to taxes, but because it is with the Department of Finance under the Deed Theft Office.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: I've lived in my building for over 11 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: Seven years ago, an individual came into the building with no paperwork, no authority, nothing, and took over the building and has harassed and beaten

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: and did everything under her power, claiming that she is a former NYPD employee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: Her name is Christine Jordan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: She has done nothing but domestically terrorize us in the building, shutting off electricity, shutting off water.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: I just got back electricity two days ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: I was without electricity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: I have taken this matter to the DA's office.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: Alvin Bragg has the case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: Courtney Vance, the case has been...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: here, Gail, since you were a Manhattan Borough President, and nothing has been done.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: That's 100 years ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: It's 100 years ago, yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: But the good thing is that we want an investigation going because I have been assaulted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: My sons were assaulted and arrested, and these people were given protection.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: Now, they have warrants out for her.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: She's never been arrested.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: This is my face, a concussion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: They kicked in the door and busted my face.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: I ended up three days in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: This is domestic terrorism, okay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: I filed with the Division of Human Rights Office.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: And finally, we have a case number 102294147.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: And it says here on July 27th,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: 2023, Cadian Presley filed a complaint with the New York State Department of Human Rights, charging the above, which is Christine Jordan, the respondent, with unlawful discriminative practice relating to housing

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: because of age, creed, origin, disability, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: And after the investigation, the division has determined that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: In its jurisdiction, in this matter, there is probable cause.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: There's probable cause exists to believe that the respondents have engaged or are engaged in unlawful discriminatory practice that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: You know, so they have been found guilty.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: And I would like for this committee to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: to look into the deed theft because this individual has no right over this building and it's still going on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: I just got back electricity, I have a disability, and this has affected my entire life.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: It's not relevant, obviously, to the topic, but deed theft is a big issue for this council, so we will be in touch.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Gail.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: Thank you to the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Jamel Henderson of Citizen Action of New York supports the tax, citing New York's extreme economic inequality. He argues the revenue could fund after-school programs, public schools, senior services, NYCHA, and immigrant communities, and urges the council not to let millionaires dictate policy.
chapters.title: Jamel Henderson testifies in support of pied-à-terre tax for public services

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Brewer and the members of this council and this important committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: My name is Jamel Henderson, and I am honored to be of service as a New York City Regional Council Chair of Citizen Action of New York, which is a proud grassroots organization that is fighting for the everyday New Yorkers as well as building community and political power.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: Citizen Action of New York supports the fair and timely implementation of the PA to tear tax and urges the council to support the city's efforts to ensure the tax is implemented.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: As you all know, the New York State suffers from the greatest economic inequality in the entire country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: The data shows it time and time again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: And despite having one of the largest economies, the New York State has a long history of under-investing in state programs and services, which has disproportionately hurt working class

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: communities, more explicitly black and brown communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: New York State is home to the highest concentration of wealth in the country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: and the deepest economic inequality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: New Yorkers worth over 30 million, which is fewer than 0.4% of the population, collectively own $6.7 trillion in wealth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: In this particular tax, we are focusing on the second home, not the primary home, and this particular revenue can bring up to $500 million.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: Think about the youth and young adults that are getting ready to go back to school that have little to no after school programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: Think about our public schools in our communities that are still waiting for funding to help improve the lives of our young people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: Think about our seniors who are no longer looking for trips and food, but looking for prescription drug policies and resources to help them to get by.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: Let's think about the infrastructure of those who, like myself, live in NYCHA and are proud to live in NYCHA and are part of the moving, shaking economic foundation of this city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: Let's think about all of those who are proud immigrants who call this city home and are working tirelessly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: To make sure that they are able to make ends meet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: This tax revenue will help the everyday New Yorkers that are in your district.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: And I want to close with this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: We, the people of New York and members of the council who you represent in us, you cannot allow the few

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: millionaires and billionaires in our city to dictate over the 8 million plus everyday hard work

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: educated people of this city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: We're tired of it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: Please stand with the people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamel Henderson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Bravin Runga of Invest in Our New York supports the tax as a step toward addressing the affordability crisis. He criticizes bad-faith attacks on the tax, notes super majorities of New Yorkers support taxing the rich, and urges swift implementation of Mayor Mamdani's agenda.
chapters.title: Bravin Runga testifies in support of tax for affordability agenda

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: Can you all hear me?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: My name is Bravin Runga.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: I'm the campaign manager with Invest in Our New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: We are the statewide coalition of over 80 organizations representing thousands of New Yorkers and millions more who support our issue,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: fighting for state-level legislation to tax the ultra-wealthy and most profitable corporations in order to fund our communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: This year, we campaigned for progressive revenue, and while we did not win everything that we wanted or New Yorkers needed,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: we supported and continue to support the pied-a-terre tax as an important step forward to generating the revenue needed to maintain the city's fiscal health and enact new programs to address the affordability crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: This tax on second homes would only affect the wealthiest homeowners, many of whom do not live in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: It taxes second, third, and fourth homes valued of over $5 million, which would raise $500 million to fund critical programs from housing to schools to sanitation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: The ultra-rich are making more money than ever before.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: Income inequality is continuing to widen, and New York remains the most income-unequal state in the country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: And these ultra-rich residents of our state just received a $12 billion

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: annual tax cut from the federal government on the back of slashing our health care, our food assistance, and our supportive housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: The ultra-rich can afford to buy multi-million dollar second and third homes while the rest of us are struggling just to survive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: Most New Yorkers can't afford their rent, their groceries, their child care, or their utility bills.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: And we know we deserve better.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: That is why we have built so much momentum for taxing the rich to keep our existing government services open and fund Mayor Mumdani's wildly popular affordability agenda.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: But the rich are fighting back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: They are launching bad faith attacks on Peta Terror, weaponizing the courts, taking advantage of this hearing process to wrap up opposition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: And criticizing its implementation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: They are doing this because they do not have valid criticisms of the substance of the law, and they know they are losing the political battle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: Poll after poll shows that super majorities of New Yorkers support taxing the rich to keep our existing services open and enact new ones to address the affordability crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: Mayor Mumdani was elected with a mandate to enact his affordability agenda by taxing the rich.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: I am heartened to hear that the majority of the council support this tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: I urge you to not let this hearing process be taken advantage of by a few bad faith actors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: I urge you to implement the tax with all due haste and to be effective governing partners with the mayor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: so we can enact his affordability agenda, keep the city's fiscal health intact, and ensure New York is a place where all of us can thrive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bravin Runga
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Lee introduces the next group: Jack Bolenbach and Robert Bertigani in person, followed by Zoom testifiers Elizabeth Valdez, Ryan Foley, Shannon Ritcher, and others.
chapters.title: Lee introduces next panel of Zoom and in-person testifiers

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you very much, and thank you, this panel.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And next is Jack Bolenbach and Robert Bertigani.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Go ahead, sir.

chapters.summary: Robert Bertagna, a 30-year homeowner, received a $52,000 surcharge notice despite being a primary resident. He calls the rollout a prototypical socialist government intrusion, warns of incremental expansion of state power, and urges the council to check the mayor's authority.
chapters.title: Robert Bertagna testifies against tax as socialist government overreach

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: Thank you, Council Member Brewer, for convening this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: My name is Robert Bertagna.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: I have come here to talk about the implementation of the pied-à-terre tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: My wife and I purchased our home 30 years ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: We raised our family there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: We have filed taxes as New York City residents for decades.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: My driver's license, voter registration, tax records, and property records all provide readily available evidence that we are New York City residents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: Yet last month, I received a letter from my government

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: telling me that my family will be subject to over a $52,000 annual pied-a-terre tax, unless I apply for an exemption and convince the city that the tax did not apply to me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: The letter

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: Or effectively said, we presume you owe us this annual $52,000.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: Now prove that you do not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: And it will be at the sole discretion of the executive branch to determine whether you should pay the tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: Every New Yorker should be appalled by this underlying principle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: The expansion of socialist state power rarely begins with government announcing that it intends to control the lives of its citizens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: It happens incrementally.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: Government assumes a little more authority.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: Citizens surrender a little bit more privacy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: And the burden gradually shifts from the government justifying its actions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: To citizens being required to justify themselves to the government.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: Like this intrusion, each new intrusion is then defended as reasonable, necessary, and insignificant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: That is precisely why this episode troubles me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: Yet even as the coercive nature of this rollout became clear, the mayor has continued to defend it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: His willingness to defend and encourage this kind of prototypical socialist government intrusion should alarm each and every one of us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: This is not simply about whether one supports or opposes an anti-free market enterprise pied-a-terre tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: It's about whether New Yorkers are prepared to accept an authoritative government that is allowed to selectively target certain citizens and require

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: I urge them to prove that the government should leave them alone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: I urge the City Council to provide the essential check on the mayor and ensure that this type of outrageous government intimidation of its citizens does not happen again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Bertagna
utterances.text: Thank you for listening and thank you for staying.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I appreciate it.

chapters.summary: Elizabeth Valdez of the Brooklyn Center for Independence of the Disabled supports the tax to fund services for disabled New Yorkers. She cites federal Medicaid cuts and argues the wealthy should pay rather than home care workers and people with disabilities.
chapters.title: Elizabeth Valdez testifies in support of tax for disability services

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Now we're going to go to the Zoom, people who are testifying.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Elizabeth Valdez is first, followed by Ryan Foley.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Elizabeth Valdez, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: My name is Elizabeth Valdez and I'm an advocate with Brooklyn Center for Independence of the Disabled, a disability-led independent living center working with people with disabilities to live the fullest life possible in the community of their choice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: We support increasing tax revenue to fund the essential services, supports, and systems used by people with disabilities and others here in New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: We especially support innovative progressive taxes that can bridge New York City's budget shortfall and support programs that will benefit disabled New Yorkers and all of us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: The tax scheme considered today would raise $500 million in desperately needed funding by taxing the residences of those who can afford to contribute to our society's social safety net.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: As you know, the federal government, through H.R.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: 1, slashed trillions of dollars from the social safety net in order to deliver the wealthiest Americans massive tax break.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: So the tax under discussion today would allow New York City to take back a small portion of that lost revenue to benefit programs that will help the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Funding from Albany has also been used to support the expansion of child care for two and three-year-olds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Early childhood programs here already have made it easier to raise children in this tremendously expensive city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: And the May of Program expansion has already directly benefited disabled children who need additional services and, of course, relieved their parents as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: This is one key step towards making New York City a fair, better place to live for everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: I would be remiss if I didn't note that the city and state both face real challenges in delivering home care and health coverage to all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Home care workers struggle to make ends meet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Stressed family caregivers provide hours of unpaid care, and people with disabilities struggle to find care that they need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: The home care crisis only continues to grow as our population ages, and more and more people need long-term care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: At the same time, over a million New Yorkers will lose their health insurance by next year due to Medicaid cuts in HR1.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: We're expecting even more cuts to health care in the next year's state budget.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: You may find yourselves facing other tough choices about taxation, but ultimately this comes down to priorities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Someone will pay for these budget gaps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Will it be those who own high-priced second homes in New York City?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Or will it be home care workers, family caregivers, older adults, and people with disabilities paying through cuts to services, hours, and wages?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Implementing the tax being considered today quickly is a significant

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: First step, addressing the budget gaps.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Ryan Foley, a condominium attorney, rejects characterization of implementation critics as bad actors. He explains that unsold condominium units subject to offering plans should be excluded property under the statute but received notices anyway, showing DOF failed to filter properly.
chapters.title: Ryan Foley testifies on excluded property issues in condo notices

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Next, we're going to go to Ryan Foley, followed by Shannon Richer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: My name is Ryan Foley.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: I'm senior counsel at the law firm Star Associates LLP, where we represent sponsors and developers of condominiums across the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: Is this an initial point or two points?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: I want to raise, mention two things before I get into the substance of my message.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: One, I would like to just

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: a record to reflect a rejection of the characterization that people here today spending two and a half hours waiting to talk about the utter failures of the implementation of this tax are bad actors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: I will set aside and I will not focus any of my time on the substance of the policy, which I do have views on, but that is not the purpose of this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: So to characterize anyone coming with

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: concerns or criticisms of the implementation as bad actors is just simply false.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: Two, before I get into the substance, I just want to also mention that I've heard a lot even from this body today about everyday New Yorkers versus wealthy or second, third home owners in New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: Really, again, that is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: Every New Yorker deserves the fair taxation and implementation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: So I want to now dive into the issues that we have seen at our firm.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: One,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: is the letters, the notice letters the department sent were sent to everybody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: They were the same letter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: It's important to recognize the statute contains two entirely different concepts under the definitions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: There is covered property and there is excluded property.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: Now, when you talk about covered property, the primary residence exemptions and some of the things we've heard today come up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: What we haven't heard at all today is excluded property.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: And under Administrative Code Section 11-3201, there's exactly two categories of excluded property under the surcharge.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: One, buildings that don't have a TCO or a CO.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: And two, the focus of my comments is unsold residential units, condominium units that are subject to the sale under an offering plan with the Attorney General.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: Those properties should never have made it on the list in the first place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: They're easy to track.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: They are registered under the condominium declaration filed with the city of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: And ACRES has all of the deed transfers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: So anything that would have appeared as new development that has not had a deed transferring should never have made it on the list anyway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: But it didn't matter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: All of the letters that went out went to everybody, including the sponsor entities that hold the unsold inventory, as well as buyers of the new development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: That as of

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: January 5th, 2026, the date on which the surcharge was fixed, that would have been excluded property.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: So, A, the fact that everybody or people that purchased or hold unsold condominium units still receive these notices is incredible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Foley
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Time expired.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Next, we're going to hear from, looks like Shannon Richter and then Mabak Thiam.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Shannon Ritchie, a Brooklyn public school teacher, supports the tax citing wealth disparities she witnesses daily. She describes empty luxury condos alongside students in shelters and argues the $500 million revenue will change lives for the better.
chapters.title: Shannon Ritchie testifies in support of tax as public school teacher

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Shannon Ritchie.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: I've lived in New York City for nearly 20 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: I'm raising my son here and I fully support a peditaire tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: It feels a bit strange to even need to write and speak on this issue when the wealth disparity in our city is so apparent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: You all see it every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: As a public school teacher in Brooklyn, I had students who lived in family shelters, learning alongside students who lived in waterfront penthouses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: Some kids would travel to faraway island resorts during winter break,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: while others I'd send home with extra snacks, even gloves and hats that I swiped from last year's lost and found, because I was worried a week away from school would mean they'd go without basic necessities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: These disparities, at least in the area where I taught and I still live, are only becoming more and more glaring.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: And we're seeing them here as people testify,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: complaining about the second homes that they own here in New York City and having to pay slightly more in their taxes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
