utterances.text: I'm not going to give you my sympathy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: Towers are going up along the river, sitting empty.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: Luxury condos sell for millions, and no one actually lives there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: Maybe I'm nosy, but it's hard to miss that the new big glass boxes behind my apartment, with soaring ceilings and tons of natural light, sold for eye-watering prices, and now they just sit empty.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: Occasionally, someone will come to clean, draw the curtains, but it's an insult that I witness daily as my husband and I search rental listings, wondering how much longer we can afford to live in this neighborhood that we've called home for decades.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: A peditaire tax feels like an obvious way to fund our most necessary public needs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: The rich will barely notice the difference.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: At most, it will be a footnote from their tax consultant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: The children who can now attend a well-funded after-school program instead of riding the bus for hours until their mom gets off work, they'll notice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: The teacher who doesn't need to cut into her food budget to buy pencils and notebooks for her students who came to the first day of school with empty backpacks, she'll notice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: The proposed $500 million will change so many lives for the better.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: We voted for this, we canvassed for this, and our city deserves this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: Please stop platforming the ultra-wealthy and those who can be bought by them, and listen to the actual New Yorkers who live here and make this city what it is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Shannon Ritchie
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Maka Cham of the Center for Independence of the Disabled supports the tax and urges the administration to dedicate revenue to affordable and accessible housing for people with disabilities. She asks the city to increase the 7% set-aside for accessible units in HPD-HDC financed housing.
chapters.title: Maka Cham testifies in support of tax for accessible housing

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Mabachi Thiam and then Alison Klempp.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: Hello everyone, my name is Maka Cham.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: I'm the Housing and Health Community Organizer at the Center for Independence of the Disabled New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: We advocate for people with disabilities in the five boroughs of New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: And we thank you, Chair Lee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Brewer, for giving us the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: So we strongly support the PRR tax surcharge,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: and that is why we appreciate the city's effort to implement the PRR tax surcharge on rich homeowners with a couple of cars to address affordable and accessible housing challenges.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: It is very disturbing to see that the mayor's administration did not show up to reply to our questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: I am asking the Mamdani administration to establish a solid percentage for disability housing investment using PRR.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: The city should increase the number of affordable and accessible apartments designed and constructed for people with mobility, vision, and hearing issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: The current policy requires 7% of certain HPD-HDC finance affordable housing units.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: To be set aside for people with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: The administration should examine whether the increased percentage set aside for people with disabilities is sufficient given the housing needs of New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: We are asking the city to collect reliable data on accessible units, vacancies, and applications to identify the unmet demands and then use that information to increase the percentage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: Regarding the transparency of the implementation of peer-to-peer search items, we hope that the administration will be fair and just in enforcing

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: all the wealthy homeowners who mostly do not live in the secondary home to pay their taxes without any exception and or favoritism.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: As it is projected to bring in more than 500 million annually, we are urging the city to strictly dedicate this revenue in more affordable and accessible housing for people with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: I will submit my written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: I know my time is very limited.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maka Cham
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Allison Klempp, a new parent in Brooklyn, supports the tax and dismisses concerns about the published list as 'pearl clutching.' She argues the revenue could fund universal child care and urges the council to prioritize working-class New Yorkers over wealthy homeowners.
chapters.title: Allison Klempp testifies in support of tax for universal child care

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Allison Klempp, then CLJ, and then Valerie Mason.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Allison Klempp.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Katie Ann Presley
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Allison Klempp.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: I'm a new parent living in Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: I have lived in New York City for 15 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: I met my husband here, and we are now raising our eight-week-old son here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: I want to be clear about why we are here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: It's not because a list of already public information was aggregated and published online.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: It's not because 17,000 people who are lucky enough to own high-value homes have to upload a PDF.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: Anyone who has tried to apply for unemployment, food stamps, WIC, or Medicaid knows the many hurdles, countless hours on the phone, and dozens of documents to provide eligibility for services they need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: need to survive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: So I believe in every homeowner's ability to upload that PDF.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: You know, once upon a time there was a big book that got sent to everyone that listed people's address and phone number.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: So this pearl clutching around the list feels quite silly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: But these concerns around the list goes to show how wealth inequality is harmful to even those at the top.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: I propose that taking measures to address that inequality would go a long way towards relieving the halves of this anxiety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: We are here to talk about a tax on second homes worth $5 million or more for non-residents, so I'm not sure why any New Yorker, regardless of their tax bracket, would oppose this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: Unless they've been committing tax fraud by claiming residency elsewhere to avoid New York income taxes, for which I have no sympathy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: None of this applies to average New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: Most average New Yorkers are renters and most of us are rent burdened.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: This tax will raise necessary city revenue from people who use our city as a playground and keep valuable excess real estate as a tax shelter or an asset to profit from.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: As a new parent, I am navigating a lot of uncharted territory.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Klempp
utterances.text: We are preparing to go back to work and figure out how to incorporate child care costs, which is nearly a second rent payment, and an albatross is an albatross around our necks.

summary: The NYC Council Committee on Governmental Operations and Finance held an oversight hearing on the rollout of the pied-à-terre tax, which applies surcharges to non-primary residence properties valued above certain thresholds.
The Department of Finance declined to testify in person due to pending litigation; Commissioner Richard Lee's written testimony was read into the record by Chair Brewer.

Dozens of public witnesses testified on both the implementation failures—privacy concerns over a 900,000-property published list, burden of proof on homeowners, and co-op collection issues—and the policy itself, with supporters urging swift implementation to fund public services.
